title: 1. The Mystery of the Empty Stomach (Hook)
text: Imagine a toy car that suddenly stops moving. What does it need? Batteries! Or think about how you feel after playing outside for a long time. You feel tired and your stomach starts to rumble. Why does this happen?

title: 2. Time to Think! (Socratic Thinking)
text: Why do you think we feel hungry? What would happen to our bodies if we didn't eat anything for a whole day?

content.title: 3. The Body Battery (Discovery)
content.description: Just like a phone needs charging, our body gets charged by the food we eat.

title: 4. The Fuel for Our Body (Reveal)
text: Food gives us Energy! It helps us grow big and strong, helps us fight off sickness, and gives us power to study and play.

question: 5. Why do we need food?
options: Only to make our stomach full
To get energy, grow, and stay healthy

content.title: 6. Think Back (Reflection)
content.text: Explain in your own words how you feel when you skip a meal. Teach your younger sibling why they need to finish their food.

title: 7. Everything Connects (Connection)
text: Just like a car needs petrol, and a plant needs sunlight and water, human beings need food. All living things need some form of food to survive.

content.title: 8. Become a Master (Mastery)
content.text: Mini challenge: Make a list of all the activities you did today that required energy from the food you ate!

title: 1. The Supermarket Secret (Hook)
text: Have you ever wondered where the milk in your glass or the apple in your hand actually comes from before it reaches the supermarket?

title: 2. Time to Think! (Socratic Thinking)
text: Does a tree drink milk? Do cows grow on trees? Where do you think different foods originate?

content.title: 3. The Two Sources (Discovery)
content.description: Food comes from two main places: Plants (like trees and farms) and Animals (like cows and hens).

title: 4. Plants and Animals (Reveal)
text: We get food from two main sources: Plants (fruits, vegetables, grains like wheat and rice) and Animals (milk, eggs, meat, and honey).

question: 5. Which of these foods comes from an animal?

content.title: 6. Look Around (Reflection)
content.text: Look at what you had for lunch today. Can you point out which items came from plants and which came from animals?

title: 7. The Farm Connection (Connection)
text: Farmers work very hard to grow the plants and take care of the animals that provide us with food. We should always be thankful for our food and never waste it.

content.title: 8. Master Chef (Mastery)
content.text: Draw a plate and draw one food item from a plant and one food item from an animal that you like to eat together.

title: 1. The Chocolate Planet (Hook)
text: Imagine a world where you only ate chocolates, chips, and ice cream for every single meal. Sounds amazing, right? But wait...

title: 2. Time to Think! (Socratic Thinking)
text: What would happen to your body if you only ate ice cream every day? Why do our parents insist we eat green vegetables?

content.title: 3. The Body Shield (Discovery)
content.description: Different foods do different jobs. Some give energy, some build muscles, and some act like a shield to fight diseases.

title: 4. A Balanced Diet (Reveal)
text: To stay healthy, we must eat a mix of different foods. This is called a Balanced Diet. We also have three main meals: Breakfast (morning), Lunch (afternoon), and Dinner (night).

content.title: Teacher's Tip
content.text: Don't forget water! Water is not a food, but it is just as important. It helps our body digest the food we eat.

content.title: Common Mistake
content.text: Many students think skipping breakfast makes them lose weight or saves time. Actually, skipping breakfast makes you feel tired and sleepy in school!

question: 5. What is the meal we eat in the morning called?

content.title: 6. Teach Your Parents (Reflection)
content.text: Explain to your parents tonight why it's important to eat different types of foods and not just your favorite snack.

title: 7. The Universal Need (Connection)
text: Across the whole world, people eat different types of foods depending on where they live and their culture. In India, we might eat Roti and Dal, while somewhere else they might eat Bread and Soup. But everyone needs a balanced diet!

content.title: 8. Plan Your Day (Mastery)
content.text: Create a menu for a perfectly healthy day. Write down what you would eat for Breakfast, Lunch, and Dinner to stay strong and healthy.
